column1: # Root-chain carrier registry: single source of truth.
# Columns (TAB-separated):
#   PS-token  variant-key  selinux_enforcing  carrier-sha256  verified-incrementals
# PS-token: the ro.build.id prefix of the device (e.g. PS7319, PS7326.3178N
#   -> PS7326). Matched by prefix against the device's ro.build.id.
# variant-key: directory under carriers/ holding libhwbinder_target.so.
#   One variant may serve several PS tokens (PS7321 and PS7326 share an
#   address; the kernel BSS layout was stable across those builds).
# selinux_enforcing: the VA the variant's NULL-write targets. Derived
#   offline from the version's OTA via tools/extract-symbols.py
#   (enforcing_setup anchor; validated 3/3 against ground truths - see
#   tools/kernel-symbols.md). NEVER guess this value.
# carrier-sha256: sha256 of carriers/<variant-key>/libhwbinder_target.so.
# verified-incrementals: comma-separated ro.build.version.incremental values
#   that have been LIVE-verified against this variant, or EMPTY for none.
#   Why this column exists: ro.build.id selects an address FAMILY, but the
#   address itself belongs to the exact kernel build. PS7319/1726 and
#   PS7319/1735 share the token -- and happened to share the address, which was
#   only established by dumping the running kernel. Treating a token match as a
#   compatibility match would let a build nobody analysed reach a kernel write,
#   so version_env.sh refuses unless the incremental is listed here (or the
#   caller sets SNUSNU_ALLOW_UNVERIFIED_BUILD=1, which is logged).
#   An empty column is not "unknown", it is "no build of this variant has been
#   live-verified"; those variants still work, but only via the explicit
#   override, which keeps the default path safe.
# All variants are built from the run-18 live-proven base (10 ms wait
# patch, docs/ENODATA-ANALYSIS.md) via stage1-root/make-carrier.py.
